changes.text: Route aliases: administrators can give any page a short route, for example #/manuals instead of #/downloads/products/manuals, on the new Route aliases administration page (#/manage/route-aliases). The short route opens the target page and stays in the address bar; built-in pages win over an alias with the same name and sites are still shown when no alias matches. Route aliases use the new RouteAlias.Read, RouteAlias.Write and RouteAlias.Delete grants, support delete, restore and permanent delete like every management page, are editable in the raw database editor and appear in the audit log by their short route. The public GET /route-aliases/resolve/{alias} endpoint returns the target of an alias, and the management endpoints live under /route-aliases.

Links of the rich text editor (sites, news and articles) can optionally open in a new tab: the link tooltip has an Open in a new tab checkbox that sets target="_blank" on the link; new links open in the same tab unless it is checked, and existing links keep their target.

Section based sites: a site can have up to 30 sections shown below its content, for example to build a landing page with pictures next to the texts. A section has an optional heading, rich text, a Normal or Accented theme (the accent colour of the site) and an optional picture with a description placed on the left or the right of the text (stacked on narrow screens). The sections are edited on the site editor (Add section, move earlier or later, Remove, picture upload), saved with every site version (POST /sites and POST /sites/{id}/versions accept a sections list, GET /sites/slug/{slug}, GET /sites/index and GET /sites/{id}/versions/{version} return it, GET /sites/settings returns maxSections) and removed with the site when it is permanently deleted. Migration AddSiteSections creates the SiteSections table.

The Roles page has a Reset grants button on the built-in roles that sets their grants back to the built-in defaults (POST /roles/{id}/reset-grants); restrictions are kept and the same access rules as editing a role apply.

The built-in Developers role now holds only the developer grants (Configuration.Read, Configuration.Manage and RawDatabase.Manage) and no longer the Read grant of every other area (migration LimitDevelopersToDeveloperGrants applies this to existing databases).

Impersonation has a single grant, Impersonation.Manage; the unused Impersonation.Read, Impersonation.Write and Impersonation.Delete grants and restrictions no longer exist (migration RemoveUnusedImpersonationGrants removes them, and their assignments, from existing databases).

The built-in Developers role of an existing database now holds the Configuration.Manage grant (migration GrantDevelopersConfigurationManage); it was only given to newly created databases, so developers could not change the settings of the web app.

Two-factor authentication: every user can protect the account with an authenticator app (TOTP, set up by scanning a QR code or typing the secret) and/or passkeys (WebAuthn security keys, phones, Windows Hello, Touch ID), managed on the new Profile > Two-factor authentication page (#/profile/two-factor). Enabling the first method generates 20 one-time recovery codes (8 random letters and numbers each, shown once and stored hashed); using a recovery code at sign in consumes it, and when the last one is used a fresh bunch of 20 is generated and shown, and the codes can be regenerated at any time. It is optional by default; set Security:TwoFactorRequired to true in security.json to require it from every user: a user without a second factor is led through the setup right after the password or the sign in link before a session starts. It works after both password and magic link (sign in and lost password) sign in: POST /sign/in/password and POST /sign/in/magiclink/redeem answer 200 with { ticket, methods, setupRequired, function } instead of the tokens, and the sign in finishes with POST /sign/in/two-factor/totp, /recovery, /passkey/options + /passkey, or (when required and not yet set up) /setup/totp + /setup/totp/confirm, /setup/passkey/options + /setup/passkey (rate limited to 10 attempts per 10 minutes per client; the 5 minute ticket is sealed with Data Protection, authenticator codes cannot be replayed and passkey counters are checked). The sign in response can contain recoveryCodes when new codes were generated. Signed in users manage it with GET /profile/two-factor, POST /profile/two-factor/totp (+ /confirm), DELETE /profile/two-factor/totp, POST /profile/two-factor/passkeys/options and /passkeys, DELETE /profile/two-factor/passkeys/{id} and POST /profile/two-factor/recovery-codes (not available in impersonation sessions; the last method cannot be removed while two-factor is required). New tables UserTotps, UserPasskeys and UserRecoveryCodes (editable in the raw database editor, secrets masked, shown with readable names in the audit log).

The sign in and sign up pages are protected by a captcha: a picture of distorted characters has to be typed in before signing in with a password, signing up, requesting a sign in link or lost password email, and resending the confirmation email. The picture is rendered by the server and a new one is requested after every attempt or with the New picture button; a challenge expires after 5 minutes and can be answered only once. New endpoint GET /captcha (rate limited to 30 requests per minute per client) returns { id, image } with image as a PNG data URI; POST /sign/in/password, /sign/in/magiclink, /sign/up/password and /sign/up/confirm/resend now require captcha: { id, answer } in the body and answer 400 with { code: "captchaInvalid" } when it is missing, wrong, expired or already used.

The title of a site can be hidden: the site editor has a "Hide the title on the page" switch, and a site saved with it shows only its carousel and content without the heading above them (for example a home page that should show only the carousel). The title is still used in lists, history and the browser. The setting is stored per version in the new HideTitle column of the Sites table (an existing site keeps showing its title), is returned as hideTitle by GET /sites/{id}/versions/{version} and the public site endpoints, and is accepted as hideTitle by POST /sites and POST /sites/{id}/versions.

Sites can use an image carousel: a slider of images with optional captions and links that moves on by itself above the content of the live page (pausing on hover, with previous and next buttons, indicators and swipe, and no automatic movement for visitors who prefer reduced motion). Using it is optional for every site: a site without images is shown as before. Developers and editors manage it in the site editor: upload images, order them, set the captions, links and the seconds per image, preview it, and remove it (soft delete) while developers can restore it or delete it permanently. Every save inserts a new version of the carousel.

The carousel has its own database model (the Carousels and CarouselSlides tables, keyed by the site and versioned), its own virtual file system kind (vfs/Carousels/<site uuid>/<image uuid>) with its own image URL (/carousels/images/<id>), and its own endpoints: GET /carousels/settings, GET /carousels/sites/{siteId} (public, only for live sites), GET and POST /sites/{siteId}/carousel (Site.Read, Site.Write), POST /sites/{siteId}/carousel/delete (Site.Delete), POST /sites/{siteId}/carousel/restore and /hard/delete (RawDatabase.Manage) and POST /carousels/images (Site.Write). The carousel follows its site when the site is deleted, restored or permanently deleted, shows up in the audit log and is editable in the raw database editor.

The limits of the carousels are settings, not fixed values: Frontend:Carousels in frontend.json has MaxSlides, MinIntervalSeconds, MaxIntervalSeconds, IntervalSeconds (the interval a new carousel starts with), MaxCaptionLength and MaxImageBytes. They can be changed on the Settings page and apply without a restart, the startup create command writes the defaults, and the site editor reads the effective values from GET /carousels/settings.
The public site response (GET /sites/slug/{slug} and GET /sites/index) now includes the id of the site.

Changes of the JSON configuration files (database.json, backend.json, email.json, security.json, frontend.json and the log levels of appsettings.json) are picked up while the application runs, whether they are saved on the Settings page or edited by hand; no restart is needed any more. This covers the email provider and its templates, the security settings (JWT, magic links, elevation, email confirmation, read-only mode), the database connection, the data directory of the uploaded files, the static frontend options and the maximum download size with its request limits. A file that is not valid JSON, or values that cannot be used, are refused: the previous values stay active and the problem is logged. Only the data protection certificate and keys, the OpenTelemetry settings and the database provider are still read at startup.

The startup create command of the behind-core tool now also generates frontend.json (site title, default locale and sites settings), and the example container compose file mounts it into the web container, so the Settings page can save it when the application directory is not writable. Existing installations run the command again with --skip-existing to get the file, then mount it.

An unexpected server error, for example a configuration file that is not writable, is now answered with a 500 Internal Server Error problem response instead of failing the error handler with an InvalidOperationException about a 404 status.

Saving a configuration file on the Settings page no longer fails with Access to the path is denied when the application directory is not writable for the container user (for example frontend.json or a bind mounted file): when the file cannot be replaced through a temporary file next to it, the file is written in place. The file itself must still be writable by the user the container runs as.

Generated TOTP secret keys are 20 bytes long (32 Base32 characters) and are stored and shown without = padding (existing padded values are still accepted and are read without the padding), because some authenticators, e.g. Bitwarden, could not use the longer padded keys; the codes are still SHA-256 based.
GET /config no longer rejects one-time codes that start with a zero: the totp query parameter is now read as text instead of a number, which dropped the leading zero of about one code in ten.

Container ready command line tools: the behind-core tool can be published as a container image (tools/publish-core-tools-container.sh) and has a new startup create command that generates security.json (data protection certificate, TOTP secret key, JWT signing key, developer elevation key and magic link secret), database.json and backend.json with all the startup secrets, can keep the existing files (--skip-existing) so it can run on every container start, and returns a non-zero exit code when a command fails.

Raw database rows are listed again: choosing a table showed No rows found because the rows were requested before the selected table was known, and the table markup was minified without its optional end tags, which broke the Knockout cell comments inside the table rows. Rows are now loaded when a table is chosen, the HTML minifier keeps the optional end tags, and the empty editor and viewer boxes are no longer shown.

Raw database row viewer: every row of the Raw database page (also of the read-only tables) has a View button that shows all the column values in full, with their types, key and sensitive markers and NULL values, and lets you browse the rows of the current page with Previous and Next, edit the row (when the table is writable) or close the viewer.

Raw database table overview: the Raw database page (#/manage/raw-database) opens with a list of every table showing its name, entity, number of rows and number of columns (and a read-only badge), clicking a table opens its rows, and an All tables button returns to the overview.

Opening the management UI in a new browser tab no longer starts signed out: the session tokens are kept in the browser local storage instead of the per-tab session storage, so every tab of the browser shares the same session, and signing in, renewing the tokens, impersonating or signing out in one tab is picked up by the other tabs immediately.

Raw database editors: developers (RawDatabase.Manage) get a Raw database page under Administration (#/manage/raw-database) that lists every table of the database (all entities, their join tables and the versioning tables, discovered from the EF Core model so every new entity appears automatically) and lets them search, sort, page, insert, edit and permanently delete the rows exactly as stored, key columns are fixed while editing, Guid keys are generated when left empty, [Sensible] columns are masked (a *** value leaves the stored value unchanged) and the AuditLogEntries table is read-only. Every raw change is recorded in the audit log (Created, Updated with the property differences, HardDeleted) in one transaction with the change. New endpoints GET /raw-database/tables, GET /raw-database/tables/{table}/rows, POST /raw-database/tables/{table}/rows, POST /raw-database/tables/{table}/rows/update and POST /raw-database/tables/{table}/rows/delete (all RawDatabase.Manage; 400 with the errors for invalid values, 409 with the reason rejected or read-only).

Users can be banned without a message: the ban message is optional on the Users page and in POST /users/{id}/ban (the reason may be missing or blank and is stored empty); the wall of shame and the Users page then show no message.

Signing in with a magic link (including the Lost your password? link) no longer answers that the email is not confirmed for users whose email is confirmed: the user lookup by id dropped the email confirmation time.

Resend confirmation email: the sign in page has a Resend confirmation email button (and the magic link page links to it when the email is not confirmed) that sends a new confirmation link to the email entered (new endpoint POST /sign/up/confirm/resend, rate limited to 3 requests per 10 minutes per client, 404 when Security.EmailConfirmation is off). The answer is 204 whether or not the account exists or is already confirmed, so it does not reveal which emails are registered.

Magic links are universal: every magic link has a Function (SignIn or LostPassword, new Function column of the MagicLinks table, existing links are SignIn). POST /sign/in/magiclink takes an optional "function" (default SignIn); the redeem response carries the function of the link. A LostPassword link is emailed with the password reset template and, once redeemed, the frontend opens the change password window (#/profile/password) automatically.

Lost password: the sign in page has a Lost your password? button that emails a magic link (same endpoint, cooldown and rate limits as POST /sign/in/magiclink); following it signs the user in and goes straight to the new password field of the Profile page (new endpoint PUT /profile/password, available to signed in users, rejected with 403 while impersonating).

The Users page shows an Email not confirmed badge and a Confirm email button for users whose email is not confirmed yet (new endpoint POST /users/{id}/confirm/email, available to everyone who can manage users and moderate the target).

When email confirmation is required (Security.EmailConfirmation), only users with a confirmed email can sign in: password and magic link sign-in answer 403 with { "code": "emailNotConfirmed" } for unconfirmed users and the sign-in pages show a message asking them to confirm their email.

A user can no longer add grants to themselves: besides being unable to edit their own access, they cannot add grants (or lift restrictions) on a role they hold themselves, not even developers. Removing grants from such a role is still allowed.

Developer grants (Configuration.* and RawDatabase.Manage) are now reserved for the built-in Developers role and for roles flagged as developer roles; administrators can never obtain, pass on or assign them or any developer role. Roles have a new IsDeveloper flag (migration AddDeveloperRoles; the Developers role and any role already holding a developer grant are flagged). Only developers can create a developer role (POST /roles with isDeveloper) or change the flag of a custom role (new endpoint PUT /roles/{id}/developer); a role cannot be unflagged while it grants developer access, and developer grants cannot be put on a role that is not flagged. The Roles page shows a Developer badge and lets developers create and toggle developer roles.

Users can choose their own language on the Profile page. A signed in user's choice is saved in the new per-user key/value settings (table UserSettings, key locale) and applies on every device; without an account it is remembered in the browser only. A user without a choice gets the browser's choice, then the site default. New endpoints: GET /locales (the available locales), GET /profile/settings and PUT /profile/settings/{key}.

The frontend is localized from JSON files: the locales folder holds one file per locale (en-US, International English, and hu-HU, Magyar), each with its official name and its messages. Files placed in wwwroot/locales override the built-in ones and add new locales. The default locale comes from Frontend:Site:DefaultLocale of frontend.json (en-US when empty) and GET /about returns it as defaultLocale. Texts missing from a locale fall back to en-US. Every page of the frontend is translated: the shell, sign in and sign up, the account pages, users, roles, audit log, settings, sites, menus, news, articles, galleries and downloads, including messages, dates and numbers in the active locale. Built-in menu items are translated by name; your own menu items, content and server data stay as they are.

The Settings page offers the available locales by their official names (for example Magyar) in a drop-down for Frontend:Site:DefaultLocale of frontend.json, and refuses a locale that has no file. Settings fields of GET /settings can now carry a list of options.

Images in the rich text editors (sites, news, articles) can be resized and placed: click an image to resize it with the size buttons or by dragging its corner handle, and place it on the left, in the center, on the right or inline with the text. The size and the placement are kept when the content is saved and shown on the public pages.

The page title, the menu title and the footer copyright come from the Frontend:Site section of frontend.json (Title and Copyright) instead of being fixed to Behind. The title defaults to Behind and the copyright is hidden when empty. GET /about also returns the title and the copyright.

The Settings page lets developers choose the log levels in appsettings.json (Serilog:MinimumLevel): a default level (Verbose, Debug, Information, Warning, Error or Fatal) and a level per source such as Microsoft.AspNetCore, which can be added and removed. Only the levels are changed; the rest of the file is kept. New endpoints: GET /settings/{file}/logging and PUT /settings/{file}/logging (Configuration.Read / Configuration.Manage). The levels apply after the application restarts.

The Settings page has a typed editor for email.json instead of raw values: choose the email provider (Logger or Smtp) and, for Smtp, fill in the server, port, SSL, sender address, authentication (none or basic with user name and password) and optional email templates. The values are validated and written as the email configuration records, the password is masked and a blank password keeps the stored one. New endpoints: GET /settings/email and PUT /settings/email (Configuration.Read / Configuration.Manage). The new provider applies after the application restarts.

The email provider of email.json was never applied: the application always fell back to the Logger sender and the SMTP options were not registered, so Smtp could not be used. The provider named by Email:Provider is now bound to its record and the SMTP options are registered.

Email:Authentication given as an object ({ "Type": "Basic", "Username": ..., "Password": ... }, the documented form) was read as no authentication, and Email:Templates were read as an empty list so custom email templates were ignored. Both are bound now; the authentication is also written as that object.

A Settings page in Administration shows the configuration files (appsettings.json, backend.json, database.json, email.json, frontend.json and security.json) as tabs and lets developers change their values. Passwords, secret keys, signing keys, tokens and connection strings are masked, and a blank box keeps the current secret. The magic link secret can be rotated, and the JWT signing key and the administrator and developer elevation secret keys can be generated (a new authenticator secret is shown once with a QR code). Reading needs the Configuration.Read grant, changing needs the new Configuration.Manage grant that the Developers role gets on new databases (grant it on the Roles page on existing ones); nothing can be changed while Security:ReadOnlyConfiguration is on. New endpoints: GET /settings, PUT /settings/{file}, POST /settings/{file}/generate and POST /settings/{file}/rotate.

The Sign in and Sign up buttons of the header can be hidden in backend.json (Backend:Accounts, for example { "SignUp": false }, both shown by default). It only changes the user interface; the web client reads the setting from the new public GET /accounts/settings.

The commenting feature can be switched off per entity in backend.json (Backend:Comments, for example { "News": false }, on by default). While it is off the comment endpoints of that entity answer 404 and the web client hides the comment counts and the comments section; existing comments are kept. The web client reads the setting from the new public GET /comments/settings.
Submitting a form (for example a search box) no longer rewrites the address of the page to / and loses the #/ part; the router used to treat every form submission as a navigation.

Downloads: a library of files kept in folders that can contain subfolders (any depth). The Downloads page shows a folder tree with opened and closed folders next to a table of the files of the chosen folder with a file type icon (a plain file icon when the type is unknown), the size, when it was uploaded and who uploaded it; the address follows the folder path, for example #/downloads/manuals/drivers. Managing is a separate page, Administration > Downloads (#/manage/downloads/<folder path>), with the same tree and table plus the folder, upload, rename, delete and restore tools. A folder has a slug (used in the path) and a display name, a file has a display name that defaults to its file name. Several files can be uploaded at once, each with its own display name. Folders and files can be renamed, deleted, restored and permanently deleted, the files are stored in the virtual file system as vfs/Downloads/<download>/<file> and are served as attachments at /downloads/files/<id>. The largest accepted file is set in backend.json (Backend:Downloads:MaxFileBytes, default 100 MB). New grant area Download (Read, Write, Delete, Manage, administration only) and a Downloads tab in the main menu.

Uploaded files (site, news and article images, gallery images and thumbnails) now live in a virtual file system: the database keeps an id and all the known metadata of every file (type, name, content type, size and the item it belongs to) and the content is stored in the data directory configured in the new required backend.json (Backend:DataDirectory) as vfs/<type>/<parent item>/<file>, for example vfs/Articles/<article>/<file>, or vfs/<type>/<file> while the file has no parent (the images of a site, news, article, category or gallery move under it when it is saved, and the news and article images have their own URLs /news/images/<id> and /articles/images/<id> like the gallery images have /galleries/images/<id>; the type is Sites, News, Articles, NewsCategories, ArticleCategories or Galleries), so the data directory has to be backed up together with the database. The migrator moves the images stored in the database so far into the data directory; run it with the same backend.json as the web application.

Galleries: a gallery has a title, an optional description, a thumbnail and images that can each have a description. Under Administration > Galleries images are uploaded in batches, the server generates a thumbnail for every image, the descriptions can be filled in before the gallery is published, the images can be reordered or removed, and the gallery thumbnail is either generated from its first images or uploaded. Galleries are versioned like articles (drafts, publishing, making an older version live) and can be deleted, restored and permanently deleted. Visitors browse the galleries list with thumbnails at Galleries and open a gallery to view its images in a large viewer.

ETag support in the web client: GET responses are remembered per signed in user together with their ETag, sent back as If-None-Match and reused when the server answers 304 Not Modified, so unchanged data is not downloaded again.
Loading spinner: a spinner is shown in the page area while the application loads, until the first page is displayed.

Letter filter and paging: the public news list can be filtered by the first letter of the title, and the menu items of a menu now have a search box, letter buttons and page buttons like the other management lists. Sub items are listed flat with the name of their parent.

The Administration entry of the user menu is now shown by role (administrators and developers by default, changeable in Administration > Menus) instead of by the grants of the user, so a user with a custom role that only holds a grant such as News.Read needs the role added to that menu item to see the link, or can open the Administration page by its address.

Menus: the top bar and the user menu are now built from the built-in main menu, and more menus (for example a footer menu shown at the bottom of every page) can be created under Administration > Menus. A menu item has a title, a URL (relative, http, https, mailto or tel), a target (current page, new tab or new window), a position, an optional parent (making it a sub item shown in a drop down) and the roles that see it: no role means everybody, including visitors, so for example the Administration entry is visible to administrators and developers only. User menu items, shown under the user name, can only be added to the main menu. Menus and items are versioned, support soft delete, restore and permanent delete (developers), and are named in the audit log. GET /menus?name=main&name=footer returns several menus in one request, filtered for the signed in user. Needs the new Menu.Read, Menu.Write, Menu.Delete and Menu.Manage grants, which administrators get by default.

QR codes: signed in users can request GET /generator/qrcode/<data> with the text to encode as base64 (the URL safe alphabet is accepted too) and get the QR code as an SVG image, for example to show the secret of a TOTP authenticator app. Invalid or too long data is answered with 400 and nothing is stored or cached.
The grants of a signed in user are refreshed every time the page is loaded, so new grants (for example Article.Read) show their administration links without signing in again.

Articles: public pages with a title, a short content and a content, grouped in their own article categories (with a header image) and searchable by title and content. Like news they are versioned with drafts, publishing, history, soft delete, restore and permanent delete for developers, but they cannot be scheduled, highlighted or commented. Read them at Articles, manage them under Administration (Article.Read, Article.Write, Article.Delete grants).

News, news categories and news comments are versioned like sites: every save inserts a new version and never changes an old one. News can be saved as a draft or published, an older version can be loaded into the editor or made live again, and the news list shows the live version only. The Ids of these entities are versioned keys.

News comments can be edited in place by their author and by holders of the News.Manage grant (administrators today, moderators when that role exists); an edited comment shows when it was edited, taken from the audit log.

Scheduled news: scheduling is optional, a news has no schedule by default and is shown as soon as it is published. With a schedule the news has a start and an optional end and is shown on the News page, opened and commented only while it is running; managers see every news with a Scheduled or Expired badge, and the news list is ordered by the start time (or the creation time without a schedule).

Highlighted news: a news can be flagged as highlighted and is then shown at the top of the news list; only one news can be highlighted, highlighting another one moves the highlight, and deleting a news removes its highlight.

News: a public News page lists the news, newest first and paged, each with its title, rich short content, author, the time it was created or last updated and its category; opening a news shows its rich content, or its short content when no content was written. The created and updated times are taken from the audit log.
News categories with a name and a header image uploaded in the administration; the News page can be filtered by category and shows the category header image.
Signed in users can comment on news; comments are paged, authors can delete their own comments and holders of the News.Delete grant can delete any comment.

News and news categories administration with the new News grant area (administration only): rich text editing with image uploads, search, first letter filter and paging, deleting, and for developers listing deleted records, restoring them and deleting them permanently.
The application starts when Security:Jwt is not configured, as the authorization services are always registered.

Licenses page linked from the footer: Behind is licensed under GPL-2.0-or-later and the page lists every frontend library, server package and development tool with its version, license and copyright, linking to the license texts.
LICENSE file with the GNU General Public License version 2 (or later) and the project copyright notice; the build properties declare the same license expression.
Confirming an email no longer ends with an incomplete link message after it succeeded; the link parameters are cleared without running the page a second time.
Sign-up sends a confirmation email with a link, and the link confirms the email address.
Email confirmation can be turned off with Security:EmailConfirmation (default true); when off, new emails are confirmed at the moment of sign-up.
Sign-up now sends (and logs) the confirmation email; the logger email sender also logs the email body when the environment is Development.
Passwordless sign-in with Magic Links, including rate limiting and security policies.
Sign-up, profile and display name management.
Session management: view the current session, list all sessions and sign out everywhere.
Role management and fine-grained access control for users and roles.
Administration area with user management: ban, unban, delete and permanently delete users.
Wall of shame listing banned users with their reason and expiry.
Elevation for sensitive operations.
Impersonation of other users, recorded in the audit log on their behalf.
Audit log with filtering, searching and paging.
Site administration: sites with a title, an editable slug and rich content (with image uploads), saved as versions that stay drafts until published, with one active version served in the wild.
Public sites are served at /<slug>, with /site/<slug> as the fallback for slugs that match built-in pages.
Sites can be searched, filtered by first letter and paged, deleted, restored and permanently deleted, like users.
Roles can be searched, filtered by first letter and paged, and deleted roles can be restored or permanently deleted by developers.
A custom index site: frontend.json can name a site slug that is shown at #/, and the Sites pages mark it.
The maximum site image size is configurable in frontend.json.
Active versions are stored in their own database context, as they are shared by every versioned entity.
Changes to frontend.json (site settings, image size limit, index site) are picked up without restarting the application.
The Stop impersonating button is visible in the dark theme.
Versioned keys now support Guid and text keys and keep their version when converted to text.
The audit log shows names (users, roles, grants, emails and so on) instead of raw identifiers.
Email confirmation tracking and an email sender with templates.
Footer with the application name and version, and this changelog page.
Frontend views now use Bootstrap, including automatic light and dark themes.
Requests are logged with correlation ids, and ETag support was added to the Web API.
Sensitive configuration values are masked, and data protection keys are protected by a certificate.
